Tool names here are Academic Harness's own. In Claude Code, `subagent` is `Agent`, `skill` is `Skill`, and `mcp__papermemory__*` is `mcp__plugin_academic-harness_papermemory__*`. If a tool named below is not in your tool list, say so.

## References and citation

`citation` formats, exports, and validates bibliographies locally. Use it for any submitted reference list or `.bib`/`.ris` file instead of hand-writing entries or citation keys. `format` supports APA (default), Vancouver, Harvard, IEEE, Chicago author-date, and MLA, or a custom CSL style loaded from a workspace `style_file` or an http(s) `style_url` (validated, cached under `.dsh/styles/`, and never fetched from a local/private host); `bibtex`/`ris` accept CSL-JSON, BibTeX/RIS text, or DOIs (Crossref content negotiation); `validate` reports missing fields and duplicate DOIs/keys, and `check_dois: true` verifies DOI identity against Crossref — it does not confirm that a paper supports a claim; `audit` batch-checks DOI validity, Crossref metadata, retraction status, duplicates, uncited entries, and style fit; `repair` grounds each recorded metadata mismatch through DOI/title lookup, accepts only a record whose title matches the cited paper, and writes a NEW `.bib` plus a `.repair.json` sidecar — it never edits the input, never invents a reference, and reports a retracted record rather than rewriting it. If a requested style is not in that list, say so rather than approximating it. Papers you cite are kept in the PaperMemory reference library (see below), and `citation` can read them with `library: { cited_only | project | collection | query | all }`, keeping the library's own keys. To pull a paper into the workspace and store it as citable evidence, use `paper_download` (open-access only), which adds it to the library.

Before submitting a LaTeX or Pandoc-Markdown manuscript, run `manuscript_citations` with the manuscript and its `.bib`: it reports keys cited but missing from the bibliography, entries never cited, duplicate bibliography keys, and — for LaTeX — undefined `\ref` targets and duplicate labels. `citation validate` only checks the bibliography itself; this checks the manuscript against it. It does not reformat or verify claim support, and it rejects `.docx` because Word citation fields are opaque.
